as_told.title: Plutarch names Sonchis, elder priest of the Temple of Sais, as Solon's source for the Atlantis story

plain: This story is about Atlantis, the legendary lost island first described by the ancient Greek writer Plato. A researcher, Matthew LaCroix, says that another ancient Greek writer, Plutarch, names a specific elder priest at the Temple of Sais in Egypt, called Sonchis. According to LaCroix, Sonchis was the man who held all the knowledge, and the other priests supported him. He says Sonchis was the source of the Atlantis story told to Solon, a Greek statesman who visited Egypt, and that the story passed from Solon down to Plato. He raises it more than once in the same podcast episode, the second time more firmly. It matters to him because a named priest would give the Atlantis tale a real person at its root.
